generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, a lot of learning by doing happens in placements and practical work. A psychology student might spend time in a clinic, a school or a research lab, carrying out real tasks under supervision. Psychology also uses work-like tasks inside the course, such as running a small study or practising an assessment, where you learn the craft of the discipline by doing it rather than only reading about it.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two psychology students, both told their module includes a placement in a mental health service.

Tom treats the placement as time away from real study. He turns up, follows instructions, and waits to be told what to do, expecting the real learning to happen later, back in lectures. The weeks pass and tasks get done, but Tom does not see the placement itself as learning.

Amara treats the placement as the learning. She takes on real tasks, watches how experienced psychologists work with clients, and notices what the setting teaches that a textbook cannot. The work is not a break from study; it is a different way of studying psychology, through doing.

Both students did the same placement. Only Amara recognised it as practice- and work-based learning: learning that comes from taking part in real work.
generatedProse.summary: Practice- and work-based learning in psychology is learning by doing: taking part in real tasks in a clinic, school, lab or work-like project, rather than only studying them from the outside. You can now explain what it is and recognise it in a psychology student's experience. The next lesson looks at the many forms it takes across different subjects.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's placement practice- and work-based learning?

items.text: She took part in real tasks and treated the experience itself as learning.
She waited until she was back in lectures to do the real learning.
She spent longer on the placement than Tom did.
She read more about the service before she started.

feedback.correct: That's right. Taking part in real tasks and learning from the experience is what makes it practice- and work-based learning.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara DID, beyond turning up or reading.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's placement was practice- and work-based learning because she took part in real tasks and learned from the experience itself.
